summary.text: Donald Norcross is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 1st District, in office since a November 2014 special election. An electrician by trade, he rose through the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and served as president of the Southern New Jersey AFL-CIO before serving in the New Jersey Assembly and State Senate. He sits on the House Education and Workforce and Armed Services Committees and ran unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary.

paragraphs.text: Born December 13, 1958, in Camden, New Jersey, and grew up in Pennsauken Township, according to Wikipedia; his House biography says he was born and raised in South Jersey.
Attended Camden County College and Rutgers University-Camden; Wikipedia lists an associate degree in criminal justice from Camden County College.
Trained as an electrician through a registered apprenticeship program and, according to his House biography, rose to become a business agent for IBEW Local 351.
Served as president of the Southern New Jersey AFL-CIO, which his House biography says he did for nearly 20 years.
Elected to the New Jersey General Assembly in 2009; appointed to fill a vacancy in the New Jersey Senate in 2010 and served there until his election to the U.S. House in 2014.
Won the Democratic primary and then both a special election to fill the remainder of Rob Andrews's term and the regular election in November 2014; he was sworn in on November 12, 2014.
Serves on the House Committee on Education and Workforce and the House Armed Services Committee, where his House biography says he is ranking member of the Tactical Air and Land Forces Subcommittee.

According to his House biography, he co-founded the Labor Caucus and the bipartisan Building Trades Caucus and introduced the No Tax Breaks for Union Busting Act, the Warehouse Worker Protection Act, and the Parity Enforcement Act.
A lifelong Camden County resident who, according to his House biography, lives with his wife Andrea; they have three adult children and four grandchildren.
